claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances.

Let me start with the basics:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! I'm inquiring about my son Alex - he's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a son named Alex who is 16 years old.

Since Alex is 16, there are special rules that apply. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He recently left school actually. He's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Since Alex has left education or training but has registered with the local careers service, he may still qualify for Child Benefit.

Let me ask you a few more questions to clarify his situation:

**How long ago did Alex leave school and register with the careers service? Was it within the last 20 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was quite recent - within the last few months. He's still in that period where he's working out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's good - so he's still within the 20-week period. Let me ask you one more important question:

**Are you currently living with Alex in the UK, or is he living with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that clarification. I have one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, pre-settled status, or are you a UK citizen/have the right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me provide you with my determination:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for your son Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 16 and has left school, but because he has registered with a government-sponsored careers service, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him for up to 20 weeks from when he left education
- Since he only left school a few months ago, he's still within this 20-week period
- You live with Alex in the UK and are a UK citizen, which means you meet the residency and responsibility requirements

**Important note:** You'll need to keep an eye on the deadline - Child Benefit will continue for 20 weeks from when he left school. If he hasn't started a job, apprenticeship, or returned to education/training by the end of that 20-week period, your eligibility would end unless his circumstances change.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
